(i) the majority of respondents reported preparation for the majority of occupational skills; (2) the majority of graduates reported preparation for most educational outcomes; and, (3) there were significant differences among graduates in terms of occupational skills and educational outcome preparation.
the self-assessment approach to educational outcomes was successful in providing a baseline for future refinement of the school’s educational programs.

(1) Pharmacy graduates were prepared to demonstrate most of the occupational skills and to acquire most of the educational outcomes identified; (2) More recent graduates rated themselves as better prepared for most occupational skills; (3) Graduates with a BS degree rated themselves better prepared for most educational outcomes; and, (4) Pharmacy graduates were not adequately prepared to demonstrate the ability to apply the principles and concepts of pharmaceutical care.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a self-reported assessment model for achievement of educational outcomes in a school of pharmacy.
the development and validation of a model to evaluate the educational outcomes of students graduating with a PharmD degree.
identifying and measuring the educational outcomes of pharmacy graduates, with the ultimate goal of improving the quality of the education provided.
